holidays.name: National Creamsicle Day
holidays.description: A day to celebrate the orange-and-vanilla frozen treat that tastes like a sunny afternoon on a stick. Peel back the wrapper, take a lick, and enjoy the creamy citrus nostalgia. Modern versions come in many flavors, from yogurt to sherbet.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial food observance that celebrates the Creamsicle, a frozen treat of orange sherbet wrapped around vanilla ice cream. It has been a summertime favorite for generations and now has its own spot on the August calendar.
holidays.funFact: The Creamsicle combines orange sherbet with vanilla ice cream, and some stores hand out freebies on the day. The flavor combo is so popular that it has inspired candies, sodas, and even candles.

holidays.name: National Navajo Code Talkers Day
holidays.description: A day to honor the Navajo men who used their native language, Diné Bizaad, to create a code the enemy never cracked during World War II. Communities mark it with ceremonies, storytelling, and a renewed commitment to keeping the language alive.
holidays.origin: President Ronald Reagan proclaimed August 14 as National Navajo Code Talkers Day in 1982. Arizona law also sets the date as an annual observance, though it is not a legal holiday.
holidays.funFact: In 2000, the original 29 Navajo code talkers received the Congressional Gold Medal. The code they developed was never broken.
